---
title: "Empirical electricity forecasting: order selection and long memory"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
    number_sections: true
params:
  n_days: 800
  h_max: 5
  p_max: 5
  q_max: 5
  bootstrap_B: 99
  fracdiff_trim: 75
  seed: 42
  remove_calendar_seasonality: true
  run_preprocessing_sensitivity: false
  save_results: false
editor_options:
  chunk_output_type: inline
---

This notebook evaluates the proposed long-memory FARMA workflow on public
electricity-demand curves. The comparison is deliberately out of sample:

- **Proposed, adaptive IC:** estimate \(d\), select \((p,q)\) using adaptive
  functional HQ, and forecast with the selected FARMA model.
- **Proposed, forecast CV:** estimate \(d\), select \((p,q)\) by rolling
  validation RMSE, and forecast with the selected FARMA model.
- **Benchmark:** impose \(d=1\), fit FAR(1), and integrate forecasts back to
  the observed scale; equivalently, use FARFIMA\((1,1,0)\).

The main outcome is
\[
  \operatorname{RMSE\ ratio}_h
  = \frac{\operatorname{RMSE}_{h,\,\text{proposed}}}
  {\operatorname{RMSE}_{h,\,\text{benchmark}}},
\]
so values below one favour the proposed workflow. The notebook never filters
or rescales the result to force this ratio below one.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
locate_project_root <- function() {
  input_path <- tryCatch(
    knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE),
    error = function(e) character(0)
  )

  has_input_path <-
    length(input_path) == 1L &&
    !is.na(input_path) &&
    nzchar(input_path)

  input_candidate <- if (has_input_path) {
    normalizePath(file.path(dirname(input_path), ".."), mustWork = FALSE)
  } else {
    NA_character_
  }

  candidates <- unique(stats::na.omit(c(
    Sys.getenv("FTS_ORDER_SELECTION_CODEX", unset = NA_character_),
    input_candidate,
    "/Users/liuchang/Desktop/FTS Order Selection codex"
  )))

  valid <- vapply(candidates, function(path) {
    identical(basename(path), "FTS Order Selection codex") &&
      dir.exists(file.path(path, "Forecasting")) &&
      dir.exists(file.path(path, "Order Selection"))
  }, logical(1))

  if (!any(valid)) {
    stop(
      "Cannot locate `FTS Order Selection codex`. Set the environment variable ",
      "FTS_ORDER_SELECTION_CODEX to that folder."
    )
  }

  normalizePath(candidates[which(valid)[1]], mustWork = TRUE)
}
```

# Dataset choice

Three public electricity sources are natural candidates:

| Candidate | Functional construction | Suitability decision |
|:--|:--|:--|
| [Adelaide electricity demand (`fds::SAelectdemand`)](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/fds/versions/1.9/topics/Electricitydemand) | 3,556 daily curves, each with 48 half-hour observations, 6 July 1997--31 March 2007 | **Screening dataset:** long history and already shaped as functional observations, but it is accepted only if long memory remains after calendar adjustment |
| [UCI ElectricityLoadDiagrams20112014](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/321/electricityloaddiagrams20112) | Daily 15-minute curves for 370 clients | Strong robustness dataset, but the compressed download is about 249 MB and client aggregation requires additional choices |
| [Open Power System Data time series](https://data.open-power-system-data.org/) | Daily curves from hourly national load | Strong robustness dataset, but country choice, daylight-saving treatment, and missing-value harmonisation must be fixed first |

The Adelaide data are screened because the observation unit is already a
daily function. Adjacent half-hours are averaged to 24 hourly values, demand
is log-transformed to stabilise its scale, and the most recent
`r params$n_days` days are retained. The chronological 60%/20%/20% split is
then used for training, validation, and testing.

By default, deterministic seasonality is estimated **only from the initial
training block**. Separate hourly regressions include weekday indicators and
the first two annual Fourier harmonics. Their fitted calendar component is
removed from training, validation, and test curves before estimating \(d\) or
selecting \((p,q)\). Because future weekday and day-of-year values are known,
the calendar component can be added back to forecasts without leakage.

## Construct daily functional observations

```{r data-preparation}
data("SAelectdemand", package = "fds", envir = environment())

X_halfhour_mw <- pmax(as.matrix(SAelectdemand$y), 1)
dates_full <- seq(
  from = as.Date("1997-07-06"),
  by = "day",
  length.out = ncol(X_halfhour_mw)
)

# Average adjacent half-hours first, then log-transform. This keeps the
# back-transformed forecasts interpretable in megawatts.
X_hourly_mw <- apply(
  array(
    X_halfhour_mw,
    dim = c(2L, 24L, ncol(X_halfhour_mw))
  ),
  MARGIN = c(2L, 3L),
  FUN = mean
)

if (params$n_days > ncol(X_hourly_mw)) {
  stop("`n_days` exceeds the number of available daily curves.")
}

analysis_index <- tail(seq_len(ncol(X_hourly_mw)), params$n_days)
X_mw <- X_hourly_mw[, analysis_index, drop = FALSE]
X_log <- log(X_mw)
dates <- dates_full[analysis_index]

train_end <- floor(ncol(X_log) * 0.60)
valid_end <- train_end + floor(ncol(X_log) * 0.20)

make_calendar_design <- function(dates) {
  weekday <- factor(as.POSIXlt(dates)$wday, levels = 0:6)
  day_of_year <- as.integer(format(dates, "%j"))

  stats::model.matrix(
    ~ weekday +
      sin(2 * pi * day_of_year / 365.25) +
      cos(2 * pi * day_of_year / 365.25) +
      sin(4 * pi * day_of_year / 365.25) +
      cos(4 * pi * day_of_year / 365.25)
  )
}

calendar_design <- make_calendar_design(dates)
calendar_coefficients <- qr.solve(
  calendar_design[seq_len(train_end), , drop = FALSE],
  t(X_log[, seq_len(train_end), drop = FALSE])
)
calendar_component <- t(calendar_design %*% calendar_coefficients)

X <- if (isTRUE(params$remove_calendar_seasonality)) {
  X_log - calendar_component
} else {
  X_log
}

data_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  quantity = c(
    "Date range", "Daily curves", "Grid points per curve",
    "Training curves", "Validation curves", "Test curves", "Preprocessing"
  ),
  value = c(
    paste(format(min(dates)), "to", format(max(dates))),
    ncol(X), nrow(X), train_end, valid_end - train_end,
    ncol(X) - valid_end,
    if (isTRUE(params$remove_calendar_seasonality)) {
      "Log demand minus training-only weekday and annual calendar component"
    } else {
      "Unadjusted log demand"
    }
  )
)

knitr::kable(data_summary, align = c("l", "r"))
```

```{r data-visualisation, echo=FALSE}
curve_data <- purrr::map_dfr(curve_days, function(day_index) {
  tibble::tibble(
    date = dates[day_index],
    hour = 0:23,

  )
})

```

# Empirical forecasting experiment

The full order grid is \(\{0,\ldots,5\}^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}\) by default.
For quick iteration, render with `p_max = 2`, `q_max = 2`; the final thesis run
should retain the default full grid. The expanding window is used because the
series is long and the aim is to estimate persistent dependence from all
available history.

```{r run-empirical-pipeline}
set.seed(params$seed)

electricity_result <- rolling_forecasting_pipeline_compact_order_method(
  X = X,
  h_max = params$h_max,
  train_ratio = 0.60,
  valid_ratio = 0.20,
  alpha_set = 0.05,
  window_types = "expanding",
  p_max = params$p_max,
  q_max = params$q_max,
  Npc = 1,
  far_pve = 0.95,
  m_const = 0.65,
  R_noise = 0,
  B = params$bootstrap_B,
  burn_in = 200,
  fracdiff_trim = params$fracdiff_trim,
  seed = params$seed,
  far_benchmark_d = 1,
  order_selection_method = "both",
  cv_order_window_type = "expanding"
)

if (nrow(electricity_result$error_log) > 0L) {
  print(electricity_result$error_log)
  stop("The empirical pipeline returned errors; inspect the table above.")
}

if (isTRUE(params$save_results)) {
  result_dir <- file.path(project_root, "Empirical Study", "results")
  dir.create(result_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(
    electricity_result,
    file.path(result_dir, "electricity_empirical_result.rds")
  )
}
```

# Point-forecast accuracy

```{r rmse-summary-functions}
summarise_point_forecasts <- function(result) {
  result$error_detail |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      horizon_statistics = purrr::map(error, function(error_matrix) {
        tibble::tibble(
          h = seq_len(ncol(error_matrix)),
          SSE = colSums(error_matrix^2, na.rm = TRUE),
          SAE = colSums(abs(error_matrix), na.rm = TRUE),
          n_forecast = colSums(is.finite(error_matrix))
        )
      })
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(
      order_selection_method,
      window_type,
      method,
      horizon_statistics
    ) |>
    tidyr::unnest(horizon_statistics) |>
    dplyr::group_by(order_selection_method, window_type, method, h) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      SSE = sum(SSE, na.rm = TRUE),
      SAE = sum(SAE, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_forecast = sum(n_forecast, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      RMSE = sqrt(SSE / n_forecast),
      MAE = SAE / n_forecast
    )
}

point_summary <- summarise_point_forecasts(electricity_result)

ratio_summary <- point_summary |>
  dplyr::select(
    order_selection_method,
    window_type,
    method,
    h,
    RMSE,
    MAE
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = method,
    values_from = c(RMSE, MAE)
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    RMSE_ratio = RMSE_farma / RMSE_far,
    MAE_ratio = MAE_farma / MAE_far,
    selector = dplyr::recode(
      order_selection_method,
      adaptive_ic = "Proposed: adaptive IC",
      cv_expanding = "Proposed: forecast CV"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(selector, h)
```

```{r rmse-ratio-table}
knitr::kable(
  ratio_summary |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      `Order selector` = selector,

      `Proposed RMSE` = round(RMSE_farma, 4),
      `Benchmark RMSE` = round(RMSE_far, 4),
      `RMSE ratio` = round(RMSE_ratio, 3),
      `MAE ratio` = round(MAE_ratio, 3)
    ),
  align = c("l", rep("r", 5))
)
```

## Dataset acceptance check

The dataset should not be retained merely because an unadjusted version gives
attractive ratios. It is accepted as the main empirical example only if the
calendar-adjusted series still shows positive fractional memory, the adaptive
structural order differs from the imposed \((1,0)\) benchmark, and forecast
performance improves across most horizons.

```{r dataset-acceptance, results='asis'}
adaptive_summary <- electricity_result$model_summary |>
  dplyr::filter(order_selection_method == "adaptive_ic") |>
  dplyr::slice(1)

acceptance_check <- tibble::tibble(
  criterion = c(
    "Positive fractional memory and d not close to one",
    "Adaptive-HQ order differs from (1,0)",
    "Adaptive-HQ RMSE ratio below one for at least 80% of horizons",
    "Forecast-CV RMSE ratio below one for at least 80% of horizons"
  ),
  passed = c(
    adaptive_summary$d_hat > 0 && abs(adaptive_summary$d_hat - 1) > 0.10,
    !(adaptive_summary$p_est == 1L && adaptive_summary$q_est == 0L),
    ratio_conclusion$horizons_below_one[
      ratio_conclusion$selector == "Proposed: adaptive IC"
    ] >= ceiling(0.8 * params$h_max),
    ratio_conclusion$horizons_below_one[
      ratio_conclusion$selector == "Proposed: forecast CV"
    ] >= ceiling(0.8 * params$h_max)
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  acceptance_check |>
    dplyr::mutate(result = dplyr::if_else(passed, "Pass", "Fail")) |>
    dplyr::select(Criterion = criterion, Result = result),
  align = c("l", "c")
)

if (all(acceptance_check$passed)) {
  cat("\n**Decision: retain this dataset as the main empirical example.**\n")
} else {
  cat(
    "\n**Decision: do not use this dataset as the main long-memory empirical ",
    "example. Continue screening other public datasets.**\n"
  )
}
```

# Forecast-curve visualisation

The next figure reconstructs forecasts from the stored test errors. The same
test origin is used for all methods, and the predictions are transformed from
log demand back to megawatts.

```{r forecast-curve-functions}
make_forecast_curve_data <- function(
    result,
    X_log,
    dates,
    horizons = c(1L, params$h_max),
    window_show = "expanding"
) {
  horizons <- sort(unique(as.integer(horizons)))
  max_h <- max(horizons)

  eligible_origins <- result$error_detail |>
    dplyr::filter(window_type == window_show) |>
    dplyr::mutate(has_horizon = purrr::map_lgl(error, ~ ncol(.x) >= max_h)) |>
    dplyr::filter(has_horizon) |>
    dplyr::count(t0) |>
    dplyr::filter(n >= 4L) |>
    dplyr::pull(t0)

  if (length(eligible_origins) == 0L) {
    stop("No test origin contains every requested method and horizon.")
  }

  t0_show <- eligible_origins[ceiling(length(eligible_origins) / 2)]

  selected <- result$error_detail |>
    dplyr::filter(window_type == window_show, t0 == t0_show) |>
    dplyr::filter(!(method == "far" & order_selection_method != "adaptive_ic"))

  order_labels <- result$model_summary |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      order_selection_method,
      model_label = dplyr::case_when(
        order_selection_method == "adaptive_ic" ~
          sprintf("Proposed: adaptive IC (%d,%d)", p_est, q_est),
        order_selection_method == "cv_expanding" ~
          sprintf("Proposed: forecast CV (%d,%d)", p_est, q_est),
        TRUE ~ order_selection_method
      )
    )

  prediction_data <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(selected)), function(i) {
    row <- selected[i, ]
    error_matrix <- row$error[[1]]

    purrr::map_dfr(horizons, function(h) {
      actual_log <- X_log[, t0_show + h]
      predicted_log <- actual_log + error_matrix[, h]

      tibble::tibble(
        horizon = h,
        hour = 0:(nrow(X_log) - 1L),
        value_mw = exp(predicted_log),
        order_selection_method = row$order_selection_method,
        method = row$method
      )
    })
  }) |>
    dplyr::left_join(order_labels, by = "order_selection_method") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      series = dplyr::if_else(
        method == "far",
        "Benchmark: FARFIMA(1,1,0)",
        model_label
      )
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(horizon, hour, value_mw, series)

  actual_data <- purrr::map_dfr(horizons, function(h) {
    tibble::tibble(
      horizon = h,
      hour = 0:(nrow(X_log) - 1L),
      value_mw = exp(X_log[, t0_show + h]),
      series = "Actual"
    )
  })

  dplyr::bind_rows(actual_data, prediction_data) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      forecast_date = dates[t0_show + horizon],
      panel = paste0("h = ", horizon, " · ", format(forecast_date)),
      series = factor(
        series,
        levels = c(
          "Actual",
          "Benchmark: FARFIMA(1,1,0)",
          unique(order_labels$model_label)
        )
      )
    )
}

forecast_curve_data <- make_forecast_curve_data(
  electricity_result,
  X_log = X_log,
  dates = dates,
  horizons = unique(c(1L, params$h_max))
)
```

# Optional preprocessing sensitivity

Calendar adjustment can materially change both the estimated memory and the
selected short-run order. The following screen is disabled by default because
it repeats the bootstrap estimator. Turn on
`run_preprocessing_sensitivity: true` when this robustness check is needed.

```{r preprocessing-sensitivity, eval=params$run_preprocessing_sensitivity}
screen_memory_and_order <- function(X_screen, label) {
  X_train <- X_screen[, seq_len(train_end), drop = FALSE]
  X_centered <- sweep(X_train, 1, rowMeans(X_train), "-")

  set.seed(params$seed)
  d_hat <- estimate_d_BC_LPWN2(
    X_centered,
    m_const = 0.65,
    R_noise = 0,
    B = min(params$bootstrap_B, 49L),
    burn_in = 200
  )$d_BC_LPWN2

  X_differenced <- if (d_hat == 0) {
    X_centered
  } else {
    t(FracDiff(t(X_centered), d_hat))
  }

  X_order <- if (d_hat == 0) {
    X_differenced
  } else {
    X_differenced[
      ,
      (params$fracdiff_trim + 1):ncol(X_differenced),
      drop = FALSE
    ]
  }

  selected <- select_order_far_full(
    X_order,
    p_max = params$p_max,
    q_max = params$q_max,
    Npc = 1
  )

  tibble::tibble(
    preprocessing = label,
    d_hat = as.numeric(d_hat),
    p_hat = selected$p_hat,
    q_hat = selected$q_hat
  )
}

preprocessing_screen <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  screen_memory_and_order(X_log, "Unadjusted log demand"),
  screen_memory_and_order(
    X_log - calendar_component,
    "Training-only calendar-adjusted log demand"
  )
)

knitr::kable(preprocessing_screen, digits = 3)
```

# Interpretation checklist

1. The dataset is useful for the thesis only if \(\widehat d\) is meaningfully
   different from the benchmark value one.
2. A selected order other than \((1,0)\) shows that the empirical short-run
   dynamics are not the imposed benchmark dynamics.
3. RMSE ratios below one must be judged across horizons, not at a single
   hand-picked forecast origin.
4. Forecast-curve plots are diagnostic examples; the aggregate rolling RMSE
   ratio is the primary performance evidence.
5. A CV order on the search boundary should be reported as a predictive choice
   and checked using a wider grid or an explicit complexity penalty.
